title: Modernize client serialization, trim transport shims, and slim public API surface
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our Python/JS/Go client libraries have accumulated multiple transport-layer shims and custom serializers across releases. This has resulted in inconsistent wire payloads, duplicated JSON (and binary) serializers, and fragile backward-compatibility code paths that increase maintenance cost and slow dependency upgrades.

Goal: Consolidate and modernize client-side serialization (stable wire format), remove legacy transport shims, and intentionally slim the public API surface so future dependency bumps and feature work are lower friction. This ticket coordinates the cross-language implementation, migration helpers, and the deprecation announcement process.

Scope:
- Replace ad-hoc serializers with a small, shared serialization contract per language (JSON schema + binary fallback where appropriate).
- Remove two legacy transport shims (legacyXHR in JS, legacy-http-adapter in Python) after providing migration helpers.
- Collapse overlapping convenience methods in public client surface (message() + createMessage -> create_message) and add compatibility aliases during a single release window.
- Bump core runtime deps where required to unlock improved JSON handling and smaller bundles (node 18+ toolchain, python 3.10+ testing matrix, go 1.20+ builds).
- Provide test vectors, e2e tests across host/dedicated/private backends, and a migration guide for customers.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: server-side protocol changes and major breaking wire-format changes that require server rollouts. Those will be handled separately if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Python, JS, and Go clients expose a documented single canonical serializer implementation per language
Legacy transport shims removed from main branches; migration helpers published in minor releases
All public API aliases remain for one release cycle with deprecation warnings in logs and docs
Automated test matrix (unit + e2e) validates parity between old and new serializers across representative prompt/response payloads
Dependency bumps validated in CI with performance regression guardrails (no >5% median token latency regression)
Migration guide and changelog entries published; SDK release notes include explicit customer guidance
notes: Design trade-off: prefer stable JSON-first contract; binary encodings only for edge performance paths to avoid long-term compatibility burden.
Plan to gate the JS bundle change behind a feature flag to measure client-side bundle size and startup impact before enabling by default.
Coordination: pair with Docs (PRD + migration guide), DevRel for community notes, and Support for triage playbook in case of customer regressions.
